subject: URGENT: WaveBank inference backpressure — sustained high tail latency & reserved throughput shortfall
messages:
From: Priyanka Shah <pri@wavebank.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: WaveBank Platform Team <ops@wavebank.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Feb 2028 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: [WaveBank] sudden latency spikes and 500s on production model — urgent

Dylan —

We started seeing a spike in 95/99 latency around 13:45 PST and a growing rate of 500s from your dedicated pool. Impacting two customer-facing endpoints (identity-verification and transaction-summarization). Our observability shows token queueing and many requests queuing for >2s; overall throughput reported by your API is well below our committed reserved throughput.

Attached are a subset of logs and a screenshot of our dashboard. Can you confirm whether this is a customer-side change or something on Redwood? We need a mitigation plan; this is affecting live transactions.

Priyanka
SRE, WaveBank

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Feb 2028 14:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [WaveBank] sudden latency spikes and 500s on production model — urgent

Quick triage notes from infra:
- Observed: sustained GPU utilization at 98–100% across the dedicated pool servicing WaveBank; backpressure at the scheduler layer has caused the request queue to grow and token wait time to increase.
- Error mode: 502/500 bursts originating in the runtime when scheduled batches exceed a kernel memory threshold; these manifest as failed in-flight requests rather than graceful queueing.
- Root cause hypothesis: a short-term burst of long-context requests (~x6 tokens per request compared to baseline) while batching heuristics selected kernels optimized for shorter sequences. This created higher per-request memory and reduced effective throughput against the pinned reserved capacity.

Immediate mitigations we’re enacting (15–45m):
1) Apply temporary kernel fallback to conservative memory kernels for the affected model version (reduces peak memory per batch).
2) Throttle/soft-limit incoming prefix lengths at the edge for WaveBank traffic (policy: cap requests > 2048 tokens and respond with a 429 + guidance).
3) Provision a burst authorization to allocate two spare GPU slots from our regional burst pool for the next 4 hours.
4) Enable an emergency degraded model (quantized variant) as fallback for high-volume endpoints (expected latency hit but better stability).

I’ve kicked off the kernel flip and the burst authorization now; Rishi will post live logs to the incident channel. We’ll monitor the 95/99 latency and error rate and update you.

-Priyom
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <pri@wavebank.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Feb 2028 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [WaveBank] sudden latency spikes and 500s on production model — urgent

Priyanka — thanks; quick customer-facing plan and asks:
- We will (A) enable the conservative kernel fallback and (B) route traffic to the quantized fallback model for the two endpoints in 10–15 minutes. Expected customer-visible change: brief elevated latency while routing (~1–2 min), then 95/99 latency should drop even if P50 rises slightly.
- We also request your sign-off to allow the burst GPU authorization for 4 hours to avoid queuing while we assess root cause. This does not alter your billing allocation for reserved capacity (we’ll note burst usage separately).

Can you confirm: approve the burst authorization now? Also, please share any customer SLAs we should be aware of for credit discussion. I’ll coordinate a follow-up exec readout after stabilization.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Shah <pri@wavebank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Feb 2028 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [WaveBank] sudden latency spikes and 500s on production model — urgent

Status update + exec ask:
- Stabilized: kernel fallback + burst slots reduced queueing; 99th latency improved from ~3.2s to ~0.9s. Error rate returned to baseline. Quantized fallback is live on identity-verification endpoint.
- Next steps: engineering will run a root-cause runbook testing the batching heuristics against longer-context traffic; we’ll follow with a permanent kernel selection and a model-profile recommendation to avoid future regressions.
- Exec ask: Marissa, please coordinate a 30-minute customer exec sync for Monday 11:00 PST to review impact, remediation, and any credit/contract adjustments. I’m flagging this for Sales/Finance review (possible one-time credit request) and for Product to evaluate a durable kernel schedule change.

Thanks everyone for the rapid response. Priyanka — can you confirm whether your team needs a post-mortem and the level of detail preferred?

—Dylan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
